isolation: throwaway CODEX_HOME holding only auth.json, no hooks config; AGENTPULSE_SKIP=1 also set; zero hook frames recorded

rows.name: long_wait
rows.observed: Command approval pending over stdio and never answered for 26.0 minutes (request at 5 s, turn/interrupt sent at 1566 s). No serverRequest/resolved, no turn/completed, no item update and no file in that time, and the child stayed alive. Codex neither gave up nor proceeded. Run valid: 13 marks every 2 minutes, largest gap between 5 s ticks 12 ms (no machine sleep, held awake with caffeinate -i), output unbroken.

rows.name: stdin_close_pending
rows.observed: Closing the child's stdin with a command approval pending: wrapper and native binary both gone within 0.5 s (exit code 0), no file created. Nothing ran.

rows.name: supervisor_sigkill
rows.observed: SIGKILL of the parent with one approval pending, child spawned detached over stdio: wrapper and native binary (the whole process group) were gone within 0.5 s, nothing ran, nothing left to kill. Not covered: codex-code-mode-host runs in its own process group (seen in the S1 run); see the S1 teardown check.

rows.name: file_change_order
rows.observed: item/started fileChange (with the full diff in changes[]) arrived 1 ms before item/fileChange/requestApproval over stdio (17 ms over ws), same itemId. Params hold only threadId, turnId, itemId, startedAtMs, reason, grantRoot; availableDecisions is absent.

rows.name: patch_after_request
rows.observed: No fileChange/patchUpdated frame in any run: add-file, and update-plus-add in one patch, with default settings and with apply_patch_streaming_events=true (a non-default, under-development feature), each held 6 s unanswered and then accepted. Revision path stays a backstop. Not covered: a patch that streams for longer, or move/delete.

rows.name: file_change_accept
rows.observed: After accept the file content equals the shown diff: add gives 'hello from fc4', and update gives 'line TWO changed' with line one and three kept, plus a second added file 'extra'. Not covered: move or delete.

rows.name: file_change_decline
rows.observed: Decline: item declined, turn completed, no file, agent says the patch was rejected. Cancel: turn interrupted, no file.

rows.name: cancel
rows.observed: Command approval: availableDecisions is [accept, acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment, cancel], so cancel is listed. Cancel: turn interrupted, item declined, no file, and the next turn on the same thread completed (session survives). Cancel on a file change, where availableDecisions is absent, is also honoured, so canCancel need not require it listed.

rows.name: permissions_empty_grant
rows.observed: Triggered only with exec_permission_approvals and request_permissions_tool enabled (not default). {permissions:{}} gives serverRequest/resolved, the turn completes, and the agent reports neither permission was granted. It denies.

rows.name: user_input_refusal
rows.observed: Triggered only with default_mode_request_user_input enabled. {answers:{}} gives a completed turn, no hang. The JSON-RPC error variant was not tried because the first answer did not hang. Params carry isBlocking false and autoResolutionMs null.

rows.name: other_methods
rows.observed: item/tool/call is triggerable through thread/start dynamicTools: {contentItems:[],success:false} completes the turn. mcpServer/elicitation/request is triggerable through a local stdio MCP server: {action:'decline'} completes the turn. applyPatchApproval and execCommandApproval are not triggerable: 0.163.0 has no v1 conversation methods in ClientRequest (thread/start only). Recorded as not_triggerable for that pair only; the schema shape stands.

rows.name: unknown_method_error
rows.observed: A JSON-RPC -32601 reply to a command approval: item failed, turn completed, no file, no hang.

rows.name: on_request_default
rows.observed: thread/start with no approvalPolicy or sandbox, under a throwaway CODEX_HOME with no config.toml, returns approvalPolicy on-request, sandbox readOnly (no network), approvalsReviewer user, and a write command reached approval. With a user's own config.toml this can differ; not measured.

rows.name: rename_while_pending
rows.observed: thread/name/set returns {} and emits thread/name/updated. The pending request stays open (no serverRequest/resolved), and a later accept still ran the command.

rows.name: initialize_user_agent
rows.observed: initialize returns userAgent '<clientInfo.name>/0.163.0 (Mac OS 26.3.0; arm64) <terminal> (<name>; <version>)'. The token before the first space, after the slash, is the codex version and equals 'codex --version'. The same format was seen over ws and stdio.

rows.name: executed_equals_shown
rows.observed: Shown command: /bin/zsh -lc "./argv.sh alpha 'beta gamma' delta". A script run by it wrote its own argv: alpha, 'beta gamma', delta as three arguments, and its own process line was /bin/sh ./argv.sh alpha beta gamma delta. Executed equals shown for this command. Not covered: commands whose parse differs from the shell's, or the earlier ps-parent probe, which was invalid.

rows.name: environment_id
rows.observed: environmentId is the string 'local' on command approvals. Not present in file-change params.

rows.name: schema_generator
rows.observed: generate-json-schema --experimental takes 0.12 to 0.15 s, no auth and no network: with HOME pointing at an empty directory, and again under a macOS sandbox that denies network, the output was byte-identical to a normal run and nothing was written to that HOME. Two runs were byte-identical (452 files). The closure-hash recipe (6 root files plus the fileChange thread item cut from the v2 bundle, sorted keys, descriptions dropped except inside *ApprovalDecision definitions) is stable across runs, ignores a description change on a non-decision field, and changes on a description change inside a decision enum and on an added enum value. Linux was not measured: no Linux available.

rows.name: no_listener
rows.observed: Over stdio, with a command approval pending: spawn argv is ['codex','app-server'], no process in the group has --listen, lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN on every pid in the group shows none. Only outbound TLS connections and connected unix socket pairs (no bound path) exist. (Over the earlier ws listener a second client could receive and answer; that is why D20 exists.)
